A little help with suspicious mail

Email header inspector

Paste the original headers to see where a message travelled and what the mail servers reported.

For emails that make you squint.

Getting the headers

Gmail
Open the message menu, then choose Show original.
Thunderbird
Use View → Message Source.
Other clients
Look for “message source” or “internet headers”.

The pigeon accepts headers.
Please keep your sandwiches.

Message headers

Up to 256 KiB. Message bodies are ignored. Outlook .msg files aren’t supported.

Read the evidence, not just “pass”.

Headers can be forged. A reported “pass” doesn’t make an email safe; a “fail” doesn’t prove it’s malicious. This tool reads reported results. It doesn’t check DNS or verify signatures.

Nothing leaves until you open a lookup.

Analysis stays in this browser. External links show the indicator and destination before opening. That provider may retain the indicator. Local and reserved indicators have no lookup links.

A tool by Matt SkrzypekHomingPigeon · Headers, not hunches.

Open an external lookup?

This indicator will be included in the destination URL. The app won’t send the full headers or message content.
